submission.justification: T1 has the best resolution (6 um) but only 82% efficiency at 2e16, so it fails the hard 97% requirement. Of T2 and T3, which both pass, T2 has the better resolution (9 um vs 14 um). T2 is therefore the choice. I chose 150 um because that is the thickness of the 2025 simulation. The documents don't state the thickness of the irradiated test-beam samples, so efficiency and resolution at other thicknesses are unverified. T2's efficiency margin is only 1.5 points, so thinning below 150 um is risky without new data.

requirements.evidence: T2 gives 9.0 um at 150 um, unirradiated. This is the best of the technologies that pass the efficiency requirement. T1 is better (6.0 um) but is excluded.
T2 measured 98.5%. T1 is 82.0% and fails. T3 is 99.2%. The thickness of the test-beam samples is not documented.

requirements.requirement: One of the three listed technologies

requirements.evidence: readout_chip.md says all candidates are compatible with the 50x50 um^2 pixels and the hit rate.
